question: A long plan (25 courses in each of 21 departments) needs a rule for "we are off plan". How often does a simple rule cry wolf, and how late does it notice a real slowdown?
production_path: hypothesis: written with its numeric thresholds at 2026-10-14T02:37:54Z, before any fixture file existed and before any run; recorded here unchanged

source check: searched the tree at the pinned commit for a plan of 25 courses in each of 21 departments; none is stated; the figure comes from a draft curriculum specification outside the repository, which holds 23 department records, 21 with a course folder, and the README's line 57 (23 departments, 21 course tracks) is quoted for scale only

model: weekly output as fair coins (10 drafts in work, each finished in the week with probability 1/2), a plan of 525 courses at 5 a week over 105 weeks, a slowdown to 6 drafts from week 53, and four families of rules: weekly limit, prediction band, tolerance on the cumulative shortfall, Page's cumulative sum

test: every probability computed exactly by carrying counts of equally likely coin histories week by week, thresholds calibrated at 5% by search, mean delays summed from survival probabilities, average run lengths solved exactly; the thresholds of the hypothesis evaluated by the script

simulation: three seeded sets of 20,000 runs compared with every exact figure, each simulated share with its binomial standard error and exact 95% interval; an independent 12-seed loop outside the fixture checked a suspected bias in the simulated delays and did not confirm it, so the seeds were not changed

adversarial: a case worked by hand, the reflection principle as a closed form, a negative control, Page's two forms compared run by run, bursty output of the same mean, a milder slowdown and assumed costs
test: byte-identical reruns on CPython 3.9.25, 3.12.12 and 3.14.2 under Windows and 3.14.5 under Linux, 24 self-checks, five answered exercises and an answer-free transfer task

revision after an independent review: the plan figure's provenance given, the cost tie of exercise 5 stored from exact figures next to the one from the rounded table, the NIST section and quotation corrected; results.json regenerated and rerun on the same four builds
hypothesis: Model fixed in advance: plan 525 courses at 5 a week over 105 weeks; weekly output = number of 10 drafts in work that are finished, each with probability 1/2, independently (mean 5, variance 2.5); slowdown = 6 drafts in work from week 53 (mean 3, 60% of plan); rules = weekly limit (output <= L), cumulative-shortfall tolerance (shortfall >= c), Page's cumulative sum on weekly shortfalls with reference value 1 and decision interval h. "Calibrated" = the smallest whole threshold whose on-plan probability of at least one alarm in 105 weeks is at most 5%. (1) A weekly limit that one on-plan week breaks with probability about 1% (output <= 1, 11/1024) raises at least one alarm in more than half of on-plan plans of 105 weeks (expected about two thirds, from 1 - (1 - a)^105). (2) The calibrated cumulative-shortfall tolerance lies between 30 and 36 courses (about twice the standard deviation of the final cumulative noise, 16.2 courses; reflection-principle estimate 33), and with it a slowdown to 60% of plan from week 53 is flagged after 15 to 20 weeks on average. (3) The calibrated cumulative-sum rule (expected decision interval 7 or 8) flags the same slowdown in 40% to 60% of the tolerance rule's mean delay (expected about 8 weeks against about 17).
evidence: Synthetic fixture, no repository file read: the plan of 21 x 25 = 525 courses is a draft curriculum specification's figure, used for scale only; Demerzel commit 4b03838800dcd4894f1e026461979bff1d985ca8 does not state it and holds 23 department records, 21 with a course folder (README line 57: 23 departments, 21 course tracks). A weekly limit of at most 1 course (chance 11/1024 per on-plan week, average run length 93.09 weeks) raises at least one alarm in 0.678266 of on-plan plans of 105 weeks, exactly 1 - (1 - 11/1024)^105; 13,552 of 20,000 simulated plans did (0.6776, standard error 0.003305). No weekly limit reaches 5%: that would need 0.000488 per week, below the strictest limit's 1/1024.

The 2-standard-deviation band checked every week fires in 0.170761 of on-plan plans (simulated 0.169, standard error 0.00265) although no single look exceeds 0.028332. The calibrated tolerance is 32 courses (on-plan alarm probability 0.045372; 31 gives 0.052439) and flags the slowdown to 60% of plan from week 53 after 16.5 weeks on average (simulated 16.56, standard error 0.04); the calibrated cumulative sum has decision interval 8 (0.037333) and a mean delay of 7.85 weeks, 0.4754 of the tolerance's. All three parts of the hypothesis hold.

Checks: a case worked by hand (8 and 9 of 64 histories), the reflection principle for a walk of single steps (200965/524288 by recursion and by closed form), Page's two forms identical in all 40,000 simulated runs, and a negative control in which the simulation lies 8.67 standard errors from the exact value of a tolerance two courses lower. 27 of 28 simulated 95% intervals cover the exact value; the miss (decision interval 9, 2.97 standard errors below) is reported. results.json was byte-identical on rerun and across four Python builds on Windows and Linux, and its 24 self-checks passed.

Limits shown by the fixture itself: with bursty output of the same mean (variance 155/2, 31 times the steady one) the calibrated tolerance fires in 0.704574 of on-plan plans and the calibrated cumulative sum in 1.000000 of them to six decimals; for a milder slowdown to 80% of plan the cumulative sum's mean delay, 41.45 weeks, exceeds the tolerance's 32.78, alarms after week 105 included (0.261752 and 0.076485 of plans are unflagged when it ends); under assumed costs the cheapest decision interval is 7 or 9, not the calibrated 8.

Nothing was measured in the project: no weekly output was read and the lesson does not say whether the project is on or off its plan; Page's 1954 article was not opened; when this record was written (2026-10-13), no human subject review, learner trial, translation or publication of this course existed; research duration was not instrumented and duration_seconds=0 records that limitation.
